A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SYNTHIA and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. All substantive material can be matched; v2's additional blank page does not create an evidence gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original automatic evaluations, a human evaluation with 36 annotators, and ablation experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original automatic and human evaluation results, ablations, and supplementary experimental findings.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same hierarchical ontology, affordance sampling, three-stage curriculum, contrastive losses, and affordance-based inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same existing-concept and generated-image datasets. Coverage of multiple-affordance synthesis, close versus distant affordances, and concept-based versus affordance-based prompts is unchanged.

E2.justification: Stable Diffusion, Kandinsky3, and ConceptLab participate in the same corresponding comparisons. The DALL-E reference comparisons and curriculum-free comparator are also retained.

E3.justification: The main 600-pair training setup, 500 held-out test pairs, four evaluation criteria, GPT-4o evaluation, and 36-annotator human study are unchanged. Appendix C reformats the rubric without changing its wording or scoring rules.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix E retain the same analyses of training-data size, number of affordances, affordance distance, curriculum learning, and prompt type. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same agreement calculations, including 67.5% inter-annotator agreement, 22.3% Cohen's kappa, and 91.25% human–automatic agreement. Run, seed, and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported scores, rankings, curves, and qualitative examples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains SYNTHIA's automatic novelty/coherence scores of 4.55/4.81 and corresponding human scores of 3.89/4.06.

T1.justification: The ontology definition, concept and affordance distance definitions, and training-loss equations in Section 3, including Equations 1–5, are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about functional coherence, visual novelty, ontology-guided composition, and curriculum learning.

C2.justification: The interpretations of baseline behavior and curriculum benefits are unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning subjective novelty judgments and incomplete ontology coverage.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D retain the same substantive prompts, data-processing instructions, baseline configurations, optimizer settings, training epochs, and UNet fine-tuning details. The code-access link is unchanged; removing the stray '[t]' marker is a typesetting correction.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to ConceptLab, ConceptWeaver, and other text-to-image research remains the same.

P1.justification: v2 reverses the first two equal-contributing authors and their email order, changes 'Kai-wei' to 'Kai-Wei', and removes a stray '[t]' in Appendix B.2. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adjusts the Appendix B.2 prompt box and reformats Appendix C with additional spacing and line breaks. It inserts an otherwise blank page 15, shifting subsequent material; figures and tables retain their content and designs.

improvement.justification: The method, scientific arguments, reproducibility information, and all supporting results are unchanged. Removing a stray marker and improving rubric spacing provide small presentation benefits, while v2 also introduces a blank page. These localized edits leave overall paper quality effectively unchanged.
